questions.stem: What two types of monomers are needed to make a polyester?

options.text: A diamine and a dicarboxylic acid
A diol and a dicarboxylic acid

questions.explanation: A polyester is formed from a diol (molecule with two -OH groups) and a dicarboxylic acid (molecule with two -COOH groups). The -OH and -COOH groups react to form ester links (-COO-), with water released as a by-product at each link.

questions.stem: Why can condensation polymers be broken down by hydrolysis but addition polymers cannot?

options.text: Condensation polymers contain ester or amide links that can be broken by water, while addition polymers have only C-C bonds

questions.explanation: Condensation polymers contain ester (-COO-) or amide (-CONH-) links that can be hydrolysed (broken by water) using acid or alkali catalysts, regenerating the original monomers. Addition polymers have only strong C-C single bonds in their backbone, which cannot be broken by hydrolysis.
